column7: Moving NotificationChannel.URL (the webhook/Slack/Teams bearer credential) to encrypted-at-rest storage in url_enc introduced three ways to lose it, all because url_enc held either an encryption envelope or raw passthrough plaintext with nothing distinguishing them. notification_channels is the ONE encrypted auth-secret column whose write path cannot refuse when storage.encryption.enabled is off -- the feature predates encryption here -- so passthrough rows genuinely exist, unlike MFASecret (BeginMFAEnrollment fails closed on AuthEncryptionActive). Consequences, each confirmed red before this fix: (a) an upgrading install's email channel carries url='' in the legacy column, the backfill's `url != ''` predicate skipped it, and the fail-closed ListNotificationChannels then errored on the WHOLE list over that one URL-less row -- taking the channel UI, the CRUD API and RunRecoverAdminAlerting down together (observed: "failed to decrypt notification channel 1 URL: ... unexpected end of JSON input" with 1 of 2 rows migrated); (b) CreateNotificationChannel's insert and its encrypt-then-persist were two untransacted writes, so an encrypt failure left a durable row with an empty url_enc -- the same broken shape as (a), reachable with no upgrade at all (observed: 1 row persisted where 0 was required); (c) a row written with encryption OFF stored raw plaintext in url_enc, so enabling encryption later left it undecryptable AND hard-failed sweepNotificationChannels at DeserializeEncryptedData -- and SweepAllTables propagates, so DEK rotation broke for EVERY table, not just this one (observed: backfill re-ran over 0 rows, then "invalid character 'h' looking for beginning of value"). Fixed by making the at-rest format self-describing: ports.WrapNotificationChannelURL/UnwrapNotificationChannelURL prefix url_enc with a one-byte format tag (absent/plaintext/encrypted), an unrecognised tag is an error rather than a guess at which half is the URL, the read path maps absent to the empty URL and refuses an envelope when no encryptor is wired, CreateNotificationChannel's two writes share one WithTransaction (so the insertNotificationChannelRow indirection that hid its second write from TestAtomicityGuard_UnclassifiedMultiWriteFunction is gone, satisfying INV-CORE-35 for the real reason), the startup backfill covers every row including url='' and upgrades plaintext-tagged rows the first time encryption is enabled, and that backfill now FAILS STARTUP instead of logging-and-continuing -- a permanently failing run of its off-to-on job would otherwise leave webhook credentials in plaintext at rest on an install that explicitly configured encryption, still reading back fine so nothing else surfaces it (same reasoning as the SecretValueEncryptionActive refusal immediately above the call site).
